title: Special Act on the Promotion of Persons Scheduled for Promotion Who Were Killed in Action or Died in the Line of Duty
full_text:
SPECIAL ACT ON THE PROMOTION OF PERSONS SCHEDULED FOR PROMOTION WHO WERE KILLED IN ACTION OR DIED IN THE LINE OF DUTY

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to prescribe special provisions concerning the Military Personnel Management Act with respect to the promotion of persons scheduled for promotion who were killed in action or died in the line of duty on or after September 1, 2001 and before March 28, 2011.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. The term "person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty" means a person who, among the persons scheduled for promotion announced pursuant to Article 31 of the Military Personnel Management Act, died on or after September 1, 2001 and before March 28, 2011 and was classified as killed in action or as having died in the line of duty pursuant to Article 54-2 of that Act.
2. The term "bereaved family" means the spouse, a lineal descendant, a lineal ascendant, or a sibling of a person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty.

Article 3 (Promotion of Persons Scheduled for Promotion Who Were Killed in Action or Died in the Line of Duty)
(1) Where a person who was killed in action or died in the line of duty is promoted pursuant to Article 30 (1) of the Military Personnel Management Act, a person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty shall be deemed to have been promoted to the rank for which promotion was scheduled, with the date immediately preceding the date of death deemed to be the date of issuance of the promotion order.
(2) A person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty may be promoted again pursuant to Article 30 (1) of the Military Personnel Management Act from the rank to which the person is deemed to have been promoted under paragraph (1). In such cases, if the person is to be promoted to the rank of general officer, the person shall undergo review by the Officer Promotion Selection Committee under Article 29 of the Military Personnel Management Act.

Article 4 (Application for Promotion) A bereaved family member of a person scheduled for promotion who was killed in action or died in the line of duty may apply in writing to the Minister of National Defense for promotion, together with relevant documentary evidence, as prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as an "application for promotion").

Article 5 (Decision on and Notification of Promotion)
(1) Notwithstanding Article 25 of the Military Personnel Management Act, the Minister of National Defense shall decide whether to grant promotion within 60 days from the date of receipt of an application for promotion, and shall notify the applicant of the decision in writing.
(2) Matters necessary for the procedures for decisions and notifications under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Objection to Promotion Decision)
(1) A bereaved family member who objects to a decision of the Minister of National Defense under Article 5 may file an objection concerning promotion with the Minister of National Defense within 30 days from the date of receipt of notice of that decision.
(2) Where an objection is filed under paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall review again whether promotion should be granted and notify the applicant of the decision in writing within 30 days from the date on which the objection was filed. In such cases, Article 5 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the review and notification procedures.

Article 7 (Period for Applications for Promotion) An application for promotion shall be filed no later than December 31, 2026. <Amended on February 27, 2026>

ADDENDUM <No. 16358, April 23, 2019>
This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDUM <No. 21389, February 27, 2026>
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
